About and Help

BarKey — Developed by Amanda Hernow. A free, offline barcode and QR scanner keyboard for Android.
Scan barcodes and QR codes directly into text fields instead of typing them by hand.
Our Privacy Commitment
100% Free
No subscriptions, purchases or paid features.
No Advertisements
No advertising or advertising SDKs.
No Tracking
No analytics, telemetry or user tracking.
No Accounts
No registration or login is required.
Works Offline
Barcode recognition takes place entirely on this device.
No Data Collection
BarKey does not upload or persist scanned barcode contents.

Decoded text is held temporarily in memory while it is processed. Preview keeps distinct values currently visible to the decoder so you can choose one; each suggestion expires shortly after it is no longer detected. Duplicate suppression keeps the most recent accepted value in the active input session and compares it during a one-second window. Safe Undo may temporarily retain the latest BarKey insertion and bounded nearby text; its context is cleared when the field or cursor context changes, a different editing action is used, the keyboard is hidden or switched, or the input session ends. Scan contents are not written to logs or persistent storage.
How to Use BarKey
1. Enable BarKey in Android keyboard settings.
2. Select BarKey as the active keyboard.
3. Tap the field where the scanned value should appear.
4. Point the rear camera at a barcode or QR code.
5. BarKey inserts the scanned value at the cursor in that field.
6. Use the editing and navigation controls to continue working.
Fast — The default mode. Prioritises quick scanning of normal, clearly printed barcodes.
Accurate — Uses additional processing for difficult, angled, damaged or inverted barcodes. It may be slower.
Tap to focus — Tap the camera preview to request focus at that location.
Torch — On supported devices, tap the flashlight icon to illuminate the scanning area.

Preview — Turn this on to see distinct detected values and choose which one to insert, especially when several codes are close together. Tap the required suggestion. Automatic insertion pauses while Preview is on; suggestions disappear when codes are no longer detected. The Java fallback may find fewer codes than ZXing-C++.

Focus — Turn this on, then drag the region over the barcode you want. Drag its corner handle to resize it: make it smaller to isolate closely placed codes, or wider for a long barcode. Long-press Focus to reset the region to the centre. BarKey decodes only inside this area. This is separate from tapping the camera preview to request autofocus and exposure. Focus uses the Java compatibility decoder for cropped frames, which may be slower and support fewer formats than the usual native-first scan. Check alignment on the camera in use.

Single Scan — Turn this on to accept one successfully inserted barcode in each text field. It is useful on serial-number or inventory forms where each field should receive one code. Move to another field to scan again; Enter or Tab does not by itself prove that focus changed. With Preview, the allowance is used only after you select a value and insertion succeeds. Some apps do not tell Android clearly when a field changes, so BarKey may not always be able to recognise the new field. Turn Single Scan off to return to continuous scanning.

Combining features — Preview and Focus work together when several codes are close together: use Focus to restrict the area, then Preview to choose a detected value. Single Scan can prevent further insertions into that field after an automatic scan or Preview selection. Fast and Accurate remain independent choices.

Undo — Safely undo the latest BarKey scan or Space insertion when bounded editor context still matches. A configured Enter or Tab suffix may submit or move focus; Undo cannot reverse that action and is available only if the same field and scan remain verifiable. Undo is disabled for password/private fields and unsafe selections.
Left / Right — Move the cursor within the current field.
Backspace — Tap to delete the selection or previous character. Press and hold to repeat deletion.
Space — Insert a space at the cursor.

Tab — Requests the Next action only when the editor explicitly advertises forward navigation. Otherwise BarKey does nothing: it does not inject a Tab key, submit the form or hide the keyboard. Chrome, WebView and other apps control focus traversal.
Enter — Perform the field action, or insert a newline in a multiline field when appropriate. Enter actions and inserted newlines cannot be undone.
Switch Keyboard — Return to the previous keyboard when Android supports it, or open the system keyboard picker.

Tab and Enter behaviour depends on the receiving application and the field. BarKey cannot control arbitrary focus traversal inside another app. Tab is intentionally a no-op unless the field advertises NEXT navigation; an app may still handle an advertised action in its own way.
Resize BarKey by dragging the small handle above the camera preview. The keyboard stays docked; its preview grows or shrinks while editing controls keep their normal size.
Permissions

BarKey requests Camera permission so it can scan barcodes and QR codes. Camera access is needed for scanning. You can deny permission or revoke it later in Android Settings; scanning will be unavailable until it is granted again.

Android may show its standard warning when you enable a third-party keyboard because an input method can receive text entered into fields. BarKey uses the active field to insert scans and performs editing actions when you request them.

BarKey’s app manifest removes Internet and network-state permissions, and source review found no app networking calls. Scanning needs no internet, account or login. BarKey does not request access to files, contacts, location or the microphone.

About BarKey

BarKey is a free Android input method that uses the rear camera to scan supported barcodes and QR codes. Recognition happens on this device. Scanned text is inserted into the active text field through Android’s input-method interface.

I create free software to make useful tools accessible without unnecessary subscriptions, advertisements, tracking or paywalls. Optional donations support my development; they do not unlock features or benefits.
